summary: Sacks explains that the favorable copyright ruling for Anthropic on pre-training inputs is legally sound, though Anthropic faces residual piracy liability for books it allegedly obtained improperly; the pre-training fair use distinction is key to US AI competitiveness.
quote: What Anthropic did is they created this large repository of books, and unfortunately some of them weren't paid for. They were pirated material. And so Anthropic is allegedly in some hot water.

summary: Jason argues OpenAI and other LLMs are displacing content subscriptions (e.g. NYT) and generating $10B/year in revenue substantially built on creators' work, making them the primary litigation target; he proposes a revenue-sharing model that would benefit both sides.
quote: ChatGPT is making $10 billion a year according to reports. They should give 30% of their revenue... to the top 1,000 newspapers, publications, podcasts, books.

summary: Jason argues LLMs are directly substituting for NYT subscriptions, eroding the paper's paid subscriber base and threatening its core business model.
quote: The need to buy a New York Times subscription is no longer necessary. You can go onto a language model and ask them... I no longer subscribe to it. I subscribe to OpenAI because I can get the same information there.
